note: RIDDLER SEAT 1 — the blade. Riddle: say the thing by seeming to praise it. Equivalents ride this shelf (Swift, Twain, La Rochefoucauld, Bierce, Moliere). Summon when the parable must sting politely.
interactions: met Swift in England 1726-28; the 'Rabelais in a good mood' quip about Swift is attributed, not certified
Lettres philosophiques (1734) imported Shakespeare into French letters, then decades of apologizing for his 'barbarism' — direct edge to the shakespeare shelf
inherits Moliere's comic stage; Twain and Bierce carry the blade into American letters
Orwell's 1946 essay on Gulliver ('Politics vs. Literature') reviews this shelf from the orwell shelf — 'uninteresting holiness' is his verdict on Swift
pd_unpulled: Voltaire: Micromegas (1752), Zadig (1747), L'Ingenue (1767), Le siecle de Louis XIV (1751), Essai sur les moeurs (1756), La Henriade (1723)
Swift: A Tale of a Tub (1704), The Battle of the Books, Journal to Stella, Drapier's Letters
Twain: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (PG74), Life on the Mississippi (PG245), A Connecticut Yankee (PG86), The Mysterious Stranger, Letters from the Earth (est. 1962 — walled)
Moliere: Tartuffe (1664), Le Misanthrope (1666), Le Bourgeois gentilhomme (1670), L'Avare (1668), Le Malade imaginaire (1673)
walled: Voltaire: Lettres philosophiques (1734) [some editions PD; keyed French edition preferred]
Voltaire: Correspondence — ~20,000 letters, the largest epistolary life-work on the roster (Besterman edition, Voltaire Foundation)
Twain: Letters from the Earth (1962, posthumous — estate)

equivalents.swift: the blade turned on institutions; Gulliver's Part IV is the clerk parable's darkest cousin
equivalents.twain: the blade turned on the river and the war; Huckleberry Finn = 'sound heart and deformed conscience'
equivalents.rochefoucauld: the blade compressed to aphorism; self-interest as the hidden organ of every virtue
equivalents.bierce: the blade as dictionary entry; definitions that kill the thing defined
equivalents.moliere: the blade on stage; hypocrisy given a costume and a cue to enter
